product.ta-dario386sx.summary: Triumph-Adler badge of the 16 MHz PCS 386SX platform, with preserved original ROMs
product.ta-dario386sx.history: Triumph-Adler sold this desktop as the Dario 386SX or P45. In November 1990 Computerwoche attributed its development and manufacture to Triumph-Adler in Germany and reported a price of about DM 4,000 with a monochrome VGA monitor and floppy drive.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.identity: Offsets 00000h–05FFFh (OVC 1.06) and 10000h–1FFFFh (Phoenix 1.14) are byte-identical to PCS 386SX. All 40,959 differing bytes lie in unused 06000h–0FFFFh padding: mostly FFh on Dario and 00h on Olivetti.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.rom_layo: Original 64 KB LOW and HIGH dumps interleave exactly into the 128 KB FULL image. BluMach loads the Dario originals, preserving their FFh erased-area state rather than normalizing it to the Olivetti image.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.bios_rev: Phoenix system BIOS 1.14 dated 30 October 1991 with 24 KB OVC video BIOS 1.06, Resident Diagnostics and tables.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.chipset: Shares the PCS 386SX board model: Headland HT101SX + HT113 + GC102-PC, IOC02, discrete TL16C451FN serial/parallel and WD37C65CJM floppy control, plus integrated PVGA1A. The Intel 80387SX was optional on the shared platform.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.verified: ROM reconstruction and executable identity are proven. The Dario uses the same corrected HT101SX + HT113 + GC102-PC implementation as the PCS 386SX and boots BIOS, Built-In Setup and MS-DOS with configured memory and IDE disks; its status is therefore the same usable partial level.
product.ta-dario386sx.technical.limitati: Partial and bootable, with the same boundaries as the PCS 386SX: chipset ownership is reconstructed without exact HT101SX/HT113 documentation, the M5L8042 ROM is missing, EMS and GC102-PC parity need validation, and broad software compatibility has not yet been tested. Brand-specific external hardware differences beyond the proven firmware/padding distinction have not been independently validated.
product.ta-dario386sx.document.olivetti: Olivetti PCS 386SX product sheet for the badge-equivalent platform
product.ta-dario386sx.document.firmware: Preserved TA Dario and Olivetti PCS 386SX version 1.14 LOW/HIGH/FULL dumps and byte-level comparison
product.ta-dario386sx.creation.disk.100m: Commercial: one 1.44 MB floppy drive + 100 MB IDE hard disk
product.ta-dario386sx.creation.disk.20mb: Commercial: one 1.44 MB floppy drive + 20 MB IDE hard disk
product.ta-dario386sx.creation.disk.40mb: Commercial: one 1.44 MB floppy drive + 40 MB IDE hard disk
product.ta-dario386sx.creation.model: Dario 386SX, 16 MHz 80386SX and integrated VGA; commercial configurations with two floppy drives or one floppy drive plus a hard disk
product.ta-dario386sx.creation.note: Same choices as the Olivetti PCS 386SX, whose firmware is identical to the Dario 386SX's: two 1.44 MB floppy drives, or one floppy drive with a 20, 40 or 100 MB IDE disk, 1 to 8 MB of RAM and an optional 80387SX. These are the PCS 386SX's documented configurations; no Dario brochure is preserved, and none of the choices has been checked on the Dario yet.
product.ta-dario386sx.creation.sound_not: User upgrades; audio untested at 16 MHz. Select one card (two ISA 16-bit slots + one ISA 8-bit). Use period DOS/native game support. Bundled software may need more RAM (SB16 multimedia: 4 MB) or different graphics; RAM is not changed automatically. GUS ACE is not a hardware SB replacement. WSS recording may need lower rates. PnP, AWE64 and unreviewed cards are omitted. AWE32 refers to voices, not bus width; unavailable pending its sample ROM and validated 386 software.
product.ta-dario386sx.creation.storage: Commercial configurations: two 1.44 MB floppy drives, or one floppy drive with a 20, 40 or 100 MB IDE hard disk
